subject.title: fix(codex): isolated cron reports Codex startup stalls

question: Should OpenClaw accept deterministic initialize-boundary proof for this availability-sensitive Codex startup change without requiring a reporter-account live OAuth recurring cron run first?
rationale: The patch is narrow and well-tested for the initialize boundary, but the production report is a Codex isolated-cron availability failure and the remaining proof gap is a maintainer risk decision rather than a mechanical code defect.

options.title: Accept deterministic lifecycle proof
options.body: Merge after normal CI if maintainers accept the real-stdio initialize stall and isolated-cron harness proof as enough for the targeted boundary.

options.title: Require live OAuth cron proof
options.body: Keep this PR open until a redacted full OpenAI OAuth isolated recurring cron/provider turn proves the reporter-shaped route end to end.

options.title: Narrow to diagnostics only
options.body: Ask for only the initialize diagnostic boundary now and leave broader Codex cron recovery or live-account behavior to the canonical issue.

recommendation.title: Accept deterministic lifecycle proof
recommendation.body: Merge after normal CI if maintainers accept the real-stdio initialize stall and isolated-cron harness proof as enough for the targeted boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest history signal for the Codex app-server lifecycle implementation under review.
